name: NY-25
label: Safe D

key_factors: Morelle holds a roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage, with $2.2 million raised versus $55,000 for McIntyre, who reports negative cash on hand
The district leans Democratic by about 10 points in partisan composition
Incumbency and the absence of any outside spending against Morelle reinforce his position
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97 percent
model.rationale: A D+10 district, Morelle's overwhelming money advantage, and markets pricing Democrats near 97 percent all point to a comfortable incumbent win; with no polls available, the forecast stays anchored to these fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a competitive race, or outside spending arriving against Morelle, would be the first sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-25 covers the Rochester area and leans Democratic by about ten points in partisan composition. Joseph Morelle, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term after first winning the seat in 2018. Republican Virginia McIntyre enters the general election with minimal financial backing and negative cash on hand, while Morelle has raised more than $2.2 million and faces no outside spending against him.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97 percent. The combination of a favorable district, incumbency, and a large resource advantage makes Morelle a strong favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
